title: The Philistines
lead: A people of Aegean origin who settled the southern coast of Canaan in the early 1100s BC and became Israel's chief rivals in the days of the judges, Saul and David. Their five cities were Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron.

sections.b: The Bible traces them to Caphtor, probably Crete (Amos 9:7; Jeremiah 47:4; Genesis 10:14). Genesis already places Philistines at Gerar in Abraham's and Isaac's time (Genesis 21:32; 26:1), which many scholars read as the name of a later people used for an earlier one. Others, such as Kenneth Kitchen, suggest an earlier group of Aegean traders from the same region, or a narrator updating an older name to the one his readers knew. Joshua lists their land as still to be taken (Joshua 13:2–3). They oppress Israel in the days of Samson, capture the ark, and kill Saul (Judges 13–16; 1 Samuel 4–6; 1 Samuel 31). David defeats Goliath of Gath, later serves Achish of Gath, and finally subdues them (1 Samuel 17; 1 Samuel 27; 2 Samuel 5:17–25). The prophets announce judgment on their cities (Amos 1:6–8; Zephaniah 2:4–7; Zechariah 9:5–7).
